text.en: Asha clapped near the hill behind her school and heard her clap again a moment later. "That is an echo," said her teacher.

Sound is produced by vibrating bodies and needs a medium to travel, so it cannot pass through a vacuum. It travels as a longitudinal wave, a disturbance with compressions and rarefactions. The speed of sound is different in solids, liquids and gases.
A sound wave has a time period, a frequency (vibrations per second), a wavelength, an amplitude and a speed. Loudness depends on the amplitude, pitch depends on the frequency and timbre is the quality that tells two instruments apart even when loudness and pitch are the same.
Sound with a frequency below 20 Hz is infrasonic and above 20,000 Hz is ultrasonic. Sound reflects from hard surfaces, and an echo is heard when the reflected sound reaches us after at least about 0.1 second. Reverberation is the persistence of sound from repeated reflections.
Ultrasonic sound is used in SONAR to find the depth of the sea and in medical scans, and the electrocardiogram records the electrical activity of the heart.

problem.en: A wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. Find its speed.

prompt.en: A friend says Sound can travel through a vacuum. How will you reply?
